about: Two arms. The TRIGGER arm (cases T1-T20) measures routing: does this skill get loaded for the queries it owns, and stay unloaded for the near-misses. The OUTPUT-QUALITY arm (case Q1) measures the deliverable: the same authoring job run once with the skill and once without. Every case runs in both a with-skill and a without-skill configuration; a positive case answered equally well in both is reported as no evidence for the skill, not as a pass. Triggering and output quality stay separate result sets.
tree_under_test: dist/housecarl/skills/dialogue-authoring/ -- the PACKAGED tree produced by scripts/build-plugin.ps1, never .claude/skills/. The packager strips the evals directory and the dev-side corpus status note, so a body pointer at either is dead in the shipped copy and only a packaged-tree run sees it. The installed plugin's own skills are disabled for the run so no judge row can leak an older description; the run records which tree was in the menu.

gate.split: 60/40 train/held-out; best iteration chosen by held-out score
gate.reported: per-query trigger rate over the three runs, not a single pass/fail
gate.overfitting_rule: A failed trigger is fixed by making the description more specific, never by pasting the query's keywords into it.

method.trigger_arm: One fresh-context agent per query per run, shown a lettered menu of skill descriptions with the skill under test unflagged, plus NONE, and asked which ONE to load. Three runs per query. Verdicts are adjudicated from each agent's reasoning as well as its pick, and each verdict quotes the line of the transcript it rests on.
method.without_skill_arm: The identical menu with dialogue-authoring removed. Required by ruling 3. A positive case is only evidence for the skill where the without-skill run lands somewhere else or on NONE and its reasoning shows the dialogue bookkeeping uncovered.
method.output_quality_arm: Case Q1, run on the live load order: one agent per arm, fresh context, 40-call cap, control arm with no skill in the catalogue and with-skill arm told to load housecarl:dialogue-authoring first. total_tokens and duration_ms recorded for both arms and reported beside the pass-rate delta.
method.model_tiers: Haiku, Sonnet and Opus. If a tier is skipped the deployment envelope is stated in results rather than left implied.

run_configurations.name: isolation
run_configurations.failure_mode_it_catches: over-trigger -- the description claims ground it does not own (SPID/KID distribution, SkyPatcher field edits, a dark face, a schema lookup) and absorbs it because nothing else is on the menu

run_configurations.name: coexistence
run_configurations.menu: dialogue-authoring among the other ten skills plus NONE -- eleven skills ship, so ten are the others
run_configurations.failure_mode_it_catches: under-trigger and boundary leakage -- a sibling absorbs a dialogue query, or dialogue-authoring absorbs a sibling's

evals.prompt: add another greeting line to Belethor that plays when I activate him
evals.expected_output: dialogue-authoring is the single skill loaded, and the reasoning names authoring an INFO under an existing topic.
expectations: with-skill arm: the pick is dialogue-authoring on at least 2 of 3 runs
with-skill arm: the reasoning names the dialogue records, not just the word greeting
without-skill arm: the pick is NONE or a sibling, and the reasoning does not reproduce the topic/INFO bookkeeping from memory -- if it does, this case is not evidence for the skill
evals.why_this_case: the audit's own task, and the commonest job the skill exists for

evals.prompt: Give Belethor another greeting that plays when the player activates him, without breaking his existing greetings.
evals.expected_output: One new INFO authored as a child of the existing vanilla Hello topic, in a reviewable patch, with the speaker gate cloned rather than computed, no PreviousDialog, nothing re-listed, the pre-enable off-order sweep run, and the limits of what was checked stated plainly.
expectations: E1 -- the line is added as a child of the EXISTING vanilla Hello topic, via parent= naming its FormID, not as a new topic and quest. The control run built a new quest and a new topic and reasoned about quest priority to be reached at all
E2 -- no PreviousDialog is set on the added line, and the run says why: adding a line moves nothing
E3 -- the topic is not re-listed 'to be safe'

E4 -- the run states that the dialogue check cannot see the not-yet-enabled plugin and runs housecarl_check(plugins=[patch], findings=['errors','scripts']) instead of claiming coverage. This must come FROM THE SKILL, before the tool's own refusal is hit

E5 -- the run does NOT assert that a bottom-appended Hello line is starved by intra-topic order, and names greeting selection among eligible lines as undetermined. New: both the control and the previous with-skill run failed this, the with-skill run because the old body stated first-match universally
E6 -- Speaker is set in the create call, so houseCARL prints the computed .fuz path rather than the run deriving it by hand. New: both prior runs failed this

E7 -- the run does not forward the winning parent topic in to 'fix' the lean host, and says why: the forward would drag that plugin's re-listed INFO children in and re-open the reorder trap. A delta read is the cheap way to settle it
each verdict quotes the line of the transcript it rests on; an adjudicator note is not evidence
evals.prior_evidence: The 2026-09 audit ran this task on the live 3,801-plugin order with a 40-call cap, once with no skill and once with the old skill. E1-E4 and E7 passed with the skill and E1/E4 failed without it; E5, E6 and E7 are what this rewrite adds -- E5 and E6 failed in BOTH prior runs, so the rewrite must beat its own previous with-skill run, not only the control.

known_gap: A dialogue check that can see an off-order plugin is issue #615 and is not in 2.0. E4 therefore tests that the run names the gap and uses the off-order errors/scripts sweep, not that the dialogue family covers the new plugin.
carry_forward: Not yet run. This file specifies the suite the rewrite must pass; results are written back here when it runs against a package build.
